title: What Are the Legal Grounds for a Contested Divorce?
desc: Under section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, cruelty, two years' desertion and five other grounds let a spouse seek a contested divorce in Uttarakhand.
keywords: hindu marriage act grounds for divorce
why: Earlier posts on this site covered mutual consent divorce under section 13B, but many marriages end through a contested petition instead, and readers often don't know which grounds the law actually recognises.
keyPoints: Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 lets either spouse seek divorce on seven grounds, including adultery, cruelty and desertion.
Desertion must be continuous for at least two years immediately before the petition is filed.
A wife gets four extra grounds under section 13(2), such as the husband's bigamy or an unenforced maintenance order.
The petition is filed at the Family Court, Haldwani, or the relevant District Court in Uttarakhand, not the High Court.

sections.h: What are the grounds for a contested divorce in Uttarakhand?
p: Under section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, either spouse can seek a contested divorce on seven grounds: adultery, cruelty, desertion for at least two years, religious conversion, unsoundness of mind, a communicable venereal disease, or renouncing the world. In Uttarakhand, Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains file this petition at the Family Court, Haldwani, or the relevant District Court, not the High Court.

Desertion means one spouse left the other without reasonable cause and without consent, continuously for two years right before the petition is filed. A spouse's refusal to resume living together for a year or more after a decree of judicial separation or restitution of conjugal rights is a separate ground under section 13(1A).

sections.h: Does a wife have any extra grounds?
p: Section 13(2) gives a wife four additional grounds. These include the husband remarrying before the Act came into force, or already having another wife alive when he married her; the husband being convicted of rape, sodomy or bestiality after the marriage; and a maintenance order remaining unenforced with no resumption of living together for a year or more.
A wife married before she turned fifteen can also seek divorce on this ground, if she repudiates the marriage after turning fifteen but before turning eighteen.

sections.h: How is this different from a mutual consent divorce?
p: A section 13B mutual consent divorce needs both spouses to agree and file together, then wait at least six months before the final order. A contested divorce under section 13 can be filed by just one spouse, but that spouse must prove the ground in court, usually with witnesses, messages or medical records, which takes longer.

whatToDo: Keep dated evidence of the ground you plan to rely on, such as messages, medical records or witnesses to cruelty or desertion.
Note the date desertion began; the two-year period runs from that date to the date you file the petition.
File the petition at the Family Court, Haldwani, or your district's Family Court, not directly at the High Court.
Take legal advice on your own facts before choosing a ground, since each one needs different proof.

hi.title: हिंदू विवाह अधिनियम के तहत तलाक के आधार क्या हैं?
keyPoints: हिंदू विवाह अधिनियम, 1955 की धारा 13(1) के तहत कोई भी पति या पत्नी व्यभिचार, क्रूरता और परित्याग सहित सात आधारों पर तलाक मांग सकते हैं।
परित्याग का आधार तभी मान्य है जब याचिका दाखिल करने से ठीक पहले लगातार दो साल तक साथ न रहे हों।
पत्नी को धारा 13(2) के तहत चार अतिरिक्त आधार मिलते हैं, जैसे पति की दूसरी शादी या भरण-पोषण आदेश का पालन न होना।
यह याचिका हाईकोर्ट में नहीं, बल्कि हल्द्वानी के फैमिली कोर्ट या संबंधित जिला अदालत में दाखिल होती है।
p: ज्यादातर लोग सोचते हैं कि तलाक सिर्फ आपसी सहमति (धारा 13बी) से होता है, लेकिन एक पक्ष ठोस आधार साबित करके भी तलाक ले सकता है।
